title: They Memorized 25,000 London Streets, Yet Their Brains Paid a Price
description:
Licensed London black-cab drivers spend two to four years memorizing 25,000 streets and 20,000 landmarks across a six-mile radius known as 'The Knowledge.' At University College London, Eleanor Maguire and colleagues showed that taxi drivers grew significantly larger posterior hippocampi than non-drivers (2000) and matched London bus drivers (2006), with a 4-year prospective MRI study proving growth occurred only in trainees who qualified—at the cost of compacted anterior hippocampal space.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Maguire EA, Gadian DG, Johnsrude IS et al. (2000) Navigation-related structural change in the hippocampi of taxi drivers. PNAS 97(8): 4398-4403. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.070039597
- Maguire EA, Woollett K, Spiers HJ (2006) London taxi drivers and bus drivers: a structural MRI and neuropsychological analysis. Hippocampus 16(12): 1091-1101. https://doi.org/10.1002/hipo.20233

AI Disclosure: Visuals and voiceover in this documentary Short were generated with AI visualization tools from peer-reviewed neuroimaging studies.
